sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year, from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
Growth peaked at 17.5% in FY2021 and 15.8% in FY2022, then slowed to 5.0% in FY2024 before recovering to 10.1% in FY2026 [D189][D238][D336][D434].
The FY2021 jump came from comparable sales up 16% and new warehouses, with e-commerce and gasoline strong, lifting revenue growth to 17.5% [P56][P54][D189].
In FY2022 comparable sales rose 14%, with inflation and gasoline, business centers and travel growing fastest, so revenue grew 15.8% [P42][D238].
FY2026 revenue growth of 10.1% came from comparable sales up 8% and sales at 25 net new warehouses [P14][D434].
Warehouse ancillary and other businesses added 3.7pp to growth in FY2026, against 0.5pp in FY2025, and now make up 20.2% of revenue [D601][D598][D599].
Food and Sundries is the largest product line at 38.5% of revenue and contributed 2.6pp of FY2026 growth [D558][D560].
Operating income grew 12.5% in FY2026, faster than revenue at 10.1%, with an incremental operating margin of 4.7% [D435][D434][D457].
Diluted shares fell 0.1%, so EPS growth of 14.0% was barely above net income growth of 13.9% [D452][D438][D436].
Operating margin of 3.9% in FY2026 is the window high, against a median of 3.4% and a low of 3.1% [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp, with SG&A adding 0.1pp and cost of revenue effectively flat [D447][D460][D459].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of net sales, though excluding gasoline price inflation it rose one basis point [P9][D460].
The largest annual gain was FY2024 at 0.3pp, led by cost of revenue at 0.4pp, helped by the absence of charter-shipping charges [D349][D361][P24].
Even so, operating margin of 3.9% sits in the 17th percentile of six retail peers, whose median is 5.0% [F32][D709][D710].
FY2026 operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income, and free cash flow of $9.38 billion was 1.02x [F82][D421][F102][D422].
Operating cash flow rose on higher operating income and a smaller net investment in inventories, from faster turns and better supplier payment terms [P6][F82].
Free cash flow margin of 3.1% is above the 2.8% window median [D418][D698].
Capex rose 17.0% against revenue growth of 10.1%, taking it to 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A [D441][D434][D417][D423].
Net cash rose to $15.1 billion in FY2026 from $9.50 billion in FY2025 [D427][D378].
Net cash of 5.0% of revenue ranks in the 100th percentile of six retail peers, whose median is -4.4% [D428][D715][D716].
Current debt rose to $2.25 billion from $75 million, while cash of $20.2 billion and a current ratio of 1.06x remain ample [X160][X159][F142][F182].
Buybacks of $848 million and dividends of $2.46 billion took 35.2% of free cash flow, leaving diluted shares at 444.4 million [X110][X120][D430][X100].
The pack lists no red-flag candidates and no data-quality checks, so the flags below come from the metrics.
Receivables grew 23.6% in FY2026, after 17.7% and 19.1% in the prior two years, far faster than revenue growth of 10.1% [D455][D406][D357][D434].
This is minor at 5 days of sales [D431], and the cited filings do not explain it, but the persistence is worth tracking.
Thin margins are the structural risk: the 3.9% operating margin trails the 5.0% peer median, so a small cost shock matters more [F32][D710].
Operating margin holding at or above the FY2026 level of 3.9% would confirm the leverage trend; a fall toward the 3.4% median would reverse it, in the FY2027 10-K [F32][D692].
Free cash flow to net income staying above 1.02x would confirm conversion; a drop below the 0.99x window median would reverse it, in the FY2027 10-K [D422][D701].
Receivable days rising beyond the FY2026 level of 5 days would confirm the build-up flagged above, in the FY2027 10-K [D431].
